Ema is building the Universal Agentic Control Plane — the layer where enterprises turn messy, human-run business processes into AI Employees that actually do the work. The platform is powerful. The bottleneck is people who can walk into a customer’s world, see what should be automated, and make it real.
That’s this role.
We’re looking for a Forward Deployed Builder to embed inside our customers and partners, find the highest-value opportunities for agentic automation, solution them, build the demo, win the deal, and then stay to implement it in production. You go in alone, Rambo in the jungle, armed with your wits, your skills, and the most powerful agentic platform on the market. We’ll train you hard before you deploy. After that, the territory is yours.
This is not a support role behind an account team. You *are* the account team, the solutions architect, and the builder, compressed into one person on the ground. Very few people in the world are doing this today. You’d be among the first.
**Where you’ll be**
Embedded, in-person, where the work is. You’d work in rotational deployments between your home office and the customers you’re embedded with across EMEA and North America. That could mean six months in London, followed by another six in Bangalore, with six more in New York. If the idea of a rotating tour across EMEA and North America lights you up, keep reading.
**What you’ll actually do**
* **Hunt for the work worth doing.** Sit inside the customer’s operation, learn how they really run, and identify the processes where agentic automation creates outsized value — the ones everyone lives with but no one has fixed.
* **Solution it.** Take a tangled, real-world business process and design it into a clean, streamlined agentic flow on Ema. You’ll make the architecture calls: which agents, which integrations, where a human stays in the loop.
* **Build the demo.** Get your hands dirty and actually build a working demo — a proof that makes the value undeniable. For partner deployments, that demo becomes *their* showcase to *their* customers, so it has to be sharp.
* **Win the technical conversation.** Read the room in the moment that matters, own every technical objection, and prove the thing works. You’re the one who makes the solution undeniable — that’s how the deal gets won.
* **Implement it.** Turn the won deal into a live, production agentic workflow the customer trusts and adopts. You own the outcome from first conversation to real usage — not a slide, not a pilot that dies, but something running.
**Who you are**
We don’t care about a rigid list of years and titles. We care that you’re:
* **Technical enough** to write some code and use our agentic platform to build a real demo - not just talk about one.
* **Persuasive enough** to read an audience and weave a captivating story that ties their pain points to Ema’s value proposition.
* **Product-minded enough** to look at a chaotic business process and see the beautiful, streamlined agentic flow hiding inside it.
* **AI-first enough** in your day-to-day to drive the impact of ten people — putting agents to work instead of grinding harder.
Most people are strong in one of these. The rare ones are formidable in all four — or hungry enough to become so. That’s who we’re looking for.
**The archetypes who would thrive in this role**
* **The Management Consultant** who wrote code at some point in their life, misses building things, and wants to step into the agentic world for real.
* **The Product Manager** who’s tired of owning a sliver and wants to live the entire journey of solving a user’s problem - from the first sales conversation all the way to adoption.
* **The Engineer** who’s ready to leave the safety of a Jira backlog and learn to navigate the chaos of a live agentic transformation
* **The Ex-Founder** who’s shelved the startup for now and wants to keep their edge sharp - craving operational freedom in an entrepreneurial environment
* **The Wildcard** who fits none of the above, but has both the burning passion and the proven skill to deliver. If that’s you, make your case.
**Why this role, why now**
Agentic AI is the biggest shift in enterprise software in a generation, and the playbook for deploying it is being written right now — by a handful of people. This is your shot to be one of them: to build the muscle, own real outcomes at real companies across two continents, and come out the other side as one of the most capable operators in the agentic world.
**We’ll make you deadly. Where you take it is up to you.**

* Maintain coverage against intelligence requirements, identifying where it should expand or deepen.
* Contribute to the taxonomy and tagging decisions that structure MENA and violent extremism data.

**Leadership and collaboration**

# Software Engineer - Python (we have office locations at Cambridge, Leeds and London)
* Full-time
* Department: Engineering
* Office: London
## Company Description
Genomics England is a global leader in enabling genomic medicine and research, focused on creating a world where everyone benefits from genomic healthcare. Building on the 100,000 Genomes Project, we support the NHS’s world-first national whole genome sequencing service and run the growing National Genomic Research Library, alongside delivering numerous major genomics initiatives. By connecting research and clinical care at national scale, we enable immediate healthcare benefits and advances for the future.
Our mission is to provide the evidence and digital systems so that by 2035 genomics could play a role in up to half of all healthcare interactions, whilst securing the UK’s position as the best place to discover, prove and benefit from genomic innovations.
We are accelerating our impact and working with patients, doctors, scientists, government and industry to improve genomic testing, and help researchers access the health data and technology they need to make new medical discoveries and create more effective, targeted medicines for everybody.
Behind the Healthcare and Research outcomes, Genomics England delivers through designing, developing and operating complex healthcare software systems.
We're on the cusp of big changes with the real prospect of genomics becoming the fabric of everyday healthcare through the lifetime - from birth to old age.
## Job Description
**Join Genomics England as a Backend Python Software Engineer**
At Genomics England, we’re looking for a Software Engineer with a demonstrable track record of delivering and owning backend software, who is passionate about making a difference in genomics and healthcare.
As an experienced Software Engineer, you’ll help build and evolve innovative products that support genomic testing, clinical decision making and research at national scale. Using your Python programming expertise and experience, you’ll directly contribute to the systems and services that enable large scale genomic research within a collaborative, supportive and empowering environment. You’ll design and develop scalable backend services, REST APIs and cloud native applications on AWS, working across databases, microservices and identity management solutions to deliver secure and reliable platforms.
You'll be joining the RE Platform team, providing software engineering expertise to our Use Research Data (URD) service. URD manages the Research Environment (RE), which is the front door to the National Genomic Research Library (NGRL), and is what our research community typically associates with Genomics England.
**Everyday responsibilities include:**
• Backend Software Development and Design. • Develop scalable, high-quality Python code following best practices. • Design and maintain microservices hosted on AWS, ensuring their reliability and efficiency. • Design, develop and maintain REST APIs for internal and external integrations. • Work with relational databases, including AWS RDS and SQL based solutions. • Support and integrate identity and access management solutions, including Okta and other Identity Providers (IdPs). • Build and enhance test automation frameworks to support robust and reliable applications. • Troubleshoot and support the resolution of issues during development and testing. • Stay informed on the latest industry trends and embrace new technologies. • Collaborate closely with front end developers, QA and Platform Engineers to create reliable, seamless solutions. • Use tools like GitLab, Confluence and Jira to support collaborative development. • Collaborate with third party suppliers to create technical specifications. • Lead feature development across the team.
**Skills and experience for success:**
• Expertise in Python and the ability to create scalable solutions. • Experienced working with AWS and microservice architectures. • Experienced with AWS services including IAM. • Experienced working with relational databases and SQL, ideally AWS RDS. • Experienced designing, developing and consuming REST APIs. • Experienced integrating with identity management and authentication platforms such as Okta or similar Identity Providers (IdPs). • Familiarity with agile methodologies and test driven development. • A proactive approach to teamwork and problem solving using collaborative tools.
**Additional Skills We’d Love to See:**
• Experienced with Amazon API Gateway, DynamoDB and Lambda. • Experienced with test automation frameworks. • Familiarity with front end React development or knowledge of JavaScript for front end applications, or a willingness to learn. • A strong understanding of code review best practices. • Experienced in mentoring and/or coaching junior team members.
**If you want your Python and backend engineering skills to directly support life changing genomic research and healthcare innovation, we’d love to hear from you. Join Genomics England and help build the systems, services and platforms that enable truly world leading genomic medicine and research, at national scale.**

BSc in Computer Science or equivalent experience

Grove is rebuilding its store. We are repositioning the entire company on Human Health — the idea that the products in your home shape the health of the people living in it. Your job is to turn that vision into a design direction concrete enough for Product and Engineering to build against — across the core flows, across the teams doing the work — and to see it through to launch.
This is the rare moment where a designer gets a blank page on a real business. Grove is a public company with millions of customers, a working commerce engine, and a leadership team that has decided to change direction. You will not spend a year building consensus for change. The change is already the mandate. Your job is to define what it looks like and get it live.
We're looking for someone who can hold the direction in one hand and a Figma file in the other. Someone who has done the rebuild before and wants to do it again with more room to swing.
**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**
**Vision and strategy for the Core-Site Experience**. In partnership with Sr. Director of Product, you will define, you will define what Grove's store should be and make that vision concrete enough that Product, Engineering, and leadership can build against it. You'll set the design principles, defend them in the room, and translate the Human Health positioning into an experience customers can feel on the first screen.

You'll make the calls on direction independently, and bring the cross-system trade-offs to your manager rather than deciding them alone.
**The core flows, end to end.** Homepage through category, search, product detail, cart, and checkout — you define how they hold together and how each one gets built. That includes the design system patterns that make the consistency real in code, designed for other people to implement, not just for you to hand off.
**AI prototyping in the design practice.** Today, strategic conversations happen against slides and get decided too late. You'll use AI prototyping in your own work every week, and partner with Engineering and the other UX Designers on the shared components and patterns that let the team put a real prototype on the table in days. When it works, we argue about a real experience early, while the argument is still cheap.
**Walk The Store.** You'll take part in the recurring series where the CEO and leadership team walk the live customer experience together, bring the design point of view into that room, and turn what surfaces there into prioritized work on the rebuild.
**Craft across the design team.** You'll mentor the designers around you, define what good looks like in practice, and raise the bar on craft. Grove should be a place where strong designers want to work, and you're a reason why.

**You prototype with AI.** You use it in your own work every week. You know what today's tools can and can't do, and you bring the rest of the design team along with you.

To achieve this, the programme will create a secure environment to store and link together regional health and care data from primary care, acute, community, social care and multi-modal sources.

King's InterHigh (KIH) is launching a new asynchronous learning product: a self-paced study offer spanning iGCSE and International A-Level courses. This is an opportunity to help shape a modern digital learning experience from the ground up — combining strong subject teaching, thoughtful curriculum design, and smart use of technology to support learners wherever and whenever they study.
We are hiring **Self-Paced Curriculum Designers** on a fixed-term basis to design, write, and build courses for **Business & Economics** — shaping the curriculum, authoring the subject content, and designing it for self-paced, online delivery. You will take the relevant iGCSE or International A-Level specification and turn it into a complete, exam-aligned course that learners can work through independently, using video, assessment, feedback, and interactive digital resources to make learning clear, engaging, and purposeful. This role is about building on strong existing subject knowledge and trusted school materials, then reimagining them for a more flexible, technology-enabled model of learning.
These are fixed-term contracts tied to course delivery, with courses to be delivered across two phases — January 2027 and September 2027.
This is a hands-on creation role with real ownership: you will help define what excellent self-paced online learning looks like for KIH, bringing together pedagogy, digital tools, media, assessment, and learner experience into courses that feel coherent, high-quality, and genuinely useful for students.
## **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**
## Write the course content
* Review, adapt, and develop existing materials to design a fully self-paced curriculum for learners
* Author lessons, explanations, worked examples, activities, and assessments to the agreed template, structure, and quality standards.
* Write to the relevant iGCSE and International A-Level specifications, exam-board requirements, and mark schemes, ensuring content is accurate, complete, and exam-aligned.
* Design a mixture of assessment — some that suits self paced learners, with auto-marked and self-checking questions giving learners instant feedback, alongside key pieces throughout the course that deliver teacher-based feedback.
## Build it for self-paced delivery
* Structure and sequence content for independent, self-paced learners with low teacher contact — using chunking, scaffolding, retrieval practice, and purposeful digital interactions to keep learners moving, thinking, and motivated without a live teacher.
* Build courses within school systems to the agreed template and brand, using the available technology to create a polished, consistent learner journey.
* Build a suite of multi-modal resources to bring courses to life — video lessons, voiceovers, screencasts, interactive tools, knowledge checks, and other digital learning assets — alongside the written material.
* Make content accessible and inclusive to all — SEND-aware, readable, with alt text and WCAG considerations applied.
## Deliver to schedule and standard
* Work to a production schedule, hitting agreed milestones for each course on a delivery-linked contract.
* Submit drafts for editorial / QA review and sign-off, and revise efficiently on feedback.
* Understand the constraints around correct licensing and developing IP — using third-party content legally and creating compliant, properly owned material that IOS can continue to use long-term.
## **THE IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:**
## Essential
* Current or recent teacher with a teaching qualification and strong subject and curriculum knowledge.
* Experience developing lesson materials for online delivery.
* Experience of asynchronous lesson design / course development.
* Understanding of how to design for independent, self-paced learners.
* Assessment design aligned to iGCSE and International A-Level specifications, exam-board requirements, and mark schemes.
* Experience working with an LMS / VLE.
* Willing and able to record video lessons and voiceovers, comfortable on camera and mic.
* Awareness of accessibility and inclusion (SEND, WCAG, readability).
* Self-motivated and self-managing — works to deadlines, comfortable working remotely and autonomously, and confident taking ownership of a course from initial specification through to finished build.
## Highly valued
* Experience of synchronous lesson design.
* Familiarity with iGCSE and International A-Level exam-board requirements and specification alignment.
* Interactive content authoring, including an interest in using digital tools to make learning more active, responsive, and engaging.
* Basic media editing
* Understanding of GDPR, copyright/licensing, and safeguarding in online education.

**Global Change Control Process**
* Owning and maintaining Jellycat's global change control process end to end, covering intake, impact assessment, prioritisation, build, testing, release and post implementation review.

# **Business Development Manager - Hellenic Systems Ltd**
**Location:** Home-based, anywhere in the UK, with regular travel to customer sites and periodic visits to our Essex head office
**About Hellenic Systems**
Founded in 1988, Hellenic Systems Ltd builds the systems that run the factory floor. Our software tells operators what to make and in what order, records what actually happened, and proves it to an auditor afterwards. The industry name for this is Manufacturing Execution Systems, or MES: the layer that sits between a company’s business systems and the machinery and people producing the goods. We design and manufacture the hardware that goes with it as well.
We are UK-based and serve over 130 sites across the UK and Europe. Our roots are in food manufacturing, particularly meat and poultry, and we are now extending into any manufacturer with the same problem to solve. A large share of what we ship is built specifically for one customer, which is why our tagline, Built Around You, is meant literally.
Our three software products are CARCASE, our kill line and livestock system, FOPS, our Factory Order Processing System, and FORMIX, our recipe and formulation management system. Our hardware includes weigh scales, touch screen terminals, outer case marking systems, carcass data capture units and label printers.
Since 2023 we have been part of Vesta Software Group, which sits within Jonas Software, an operating group of Constellation Software Inc. Constellation is one of the largest acquirers of vertical market software businesses in the world.
We are also unusually far along with AI for a business our size. It is embedded in how we build software and how we work day to day, not run as a side project, and we expect everyone here to use it.
**The Opportunity**
FORMIX, our recipe and formulation management system, has been rebuilt as a new product and is our main new business push. It guides operators through ingredient weigh-up, enforces tolerances, captures batch and operator evidence, and connects to shop floor weighing and labelling hardware. The buyers are food and drink manufacturers who still run weigh-up on paper, spreadsheets or an awkward ERP screen, and who are under real pressure on allergen control, traceability and waste.
This is a new role. It exists to build and convert a new business pipeline that does not depend on our existing account base.
**Job Summary**
The Business Development Manager owns new business at Hellenic. The role is targeted on winning new named clients and new sites, starting with FORMIX and broadening into our wider software and hardware portfolio as the pipeline develops. It is a hunting role: self-generated prospecting, campaigns and networking, then running the opportunity through demonstration, proposal, negotiation and close, with support from our technical and commercial teams.
The BDM reports to the Head of Commercial and works alongside our Account Managers, who own existing customer relationships. Growth inside existing accounts stays with them. Anything genuinely new belongs to the BDM.
**Key Responsibilities**
1. New Business Generation
* Win new named clients and new sites, principally for FORMIX in year one, broadening into CARCASE, FOPS, hardware and bespoke development as the pipeline matures.
* Generate the majority of your own pipeline through outbound prospecting, cold calling, email and LinkedIn campaigns, trade events and industry networking. Marketing and referral leads will supplement this, not replace it.
* Work the named FORMIX prospect list and the wider addressable market, including manufacturers outside our traditional meat and poultry base, such as bakery, dairy, ready meals, sauces, seasonings, flavourings and beverages.
* Open the first opportunities in adjacent sectors as we extend the product into adjacent sectors, and feed what you learn back into product and pricing.
* Qualify hard and early. We would rather have a smaller pipeline we believe in than a large one we do not.
2. Selling and Closing
* Run the full sales cycle: discovery, on-site assessment, demonstration (in person and remote), proposal, commercial negotiation and close.
* Build the business case in the customer’s language: reduced giveaway and waste, right first time batches, allergen control, audit-ready evidence and labour saved on the weigh-up line.
* Prepare and present quotations and proposals that reflect our pricing model, including site-level and tiered packaging.
* Present our solution accurately and never oversell what the product does. Where a requirement needs bespoke development, involve the technical team for scope.
* Hand over cleanly to Projects and Support at the point of sale, including a written summary of what has been sold and what the customer expects.
3. Market, Product and Competitor Knowledge
* Build and hold working knowledge of the FORMIX proposition and enough of the wider portfolio to spot an opportunity when a customer describes a problem.
* Know the competition. Be able to explain where we win and where we do not.
* Gather field intelligence on competitor pricing, bundling and contract terms.
* Track sector trends, regulation and retailer or certification pressures (for example BRCGS) that create a reason for customers to act.
4. Pipeline, CRM and Reporting
* Build and maintain a qualified pipeline of sufficient size and quality to deliver the agreed targets, with realistic close dates and values.
* Keep CRM current and accurate. Every opportunity, activity, contact and next step is logged.
* Report weekly on activity, pipeline movement and forecast, and present your numbers at commercial reviews.
* Learn and follow the company sales guidelines and standard operating procedures, and help improve our proposal and correspondence templates as you go.
* Use AI tools in your daily workflow: prospect and account research, first-draft proposals and follow-ups, call preparation and pipeline analysis. We will give you the tools and the training.
5. Working With the Team
* Work with the Account Managers so that new business and account growth do not collide, and pass leads to them where an opportunity sits inside an existing relationship.
* Work with Development, Projects and Support on solution scoping, demonstrations and delivery expectations.
* Contribute to campaigns, marketing content, case studies and event planning.
* Attend training to keep product, sector and sales skills current, and take part in team meetings and reviews.
* Carry out other reasonable duties related to the promotion, sale and delivery of our products as directed by the management team.
Targets and Measures of Success
You will carry a personal new business target, set annually with the Head of Commercial and reviewed each quarter. It covers new order value, new recurring revenue and a minimum number of genuinely new clients, and it is supported by activity and pipeline coverage measures and by the quality of what you put into the CRM.
The targets are built from our FORMIX commercial plan and are deliberately achievable for someone who prospects properly. We will share the detail, including the numbers and how the commission scheme works against them, at the interview stage.
**Qualifications and Experience**
Essential
* Proven track record of winning new business in a B2B environment, carrying and hitting a personal new business target.
* Experience selling a considered purchase with a multi-month sales cycle and more than one decision maker, typically operations, quality, engineering, IT and finance.
* Comfortable self-generating pipeline.
* Able to hold a credible conversation on a factory floor and translate an operational problem into a commercial proposal.
* Strong written, verbal and presentation skills, including the ability to write a proposal that stands on its own.
* Strong negotiation and closing skills, with the discipline to protect margin.
* Confident with CRM discipline and accurate forecasting.
* Comfortable using AI tools as part of your working day. You do not need to be technical, but you do need to be someone who reaches for them rather than avoids them.
* Full UK driving licence, and willing to travel across the UK, including overnight stays. Most of our target market sits in a band from the Midlands up through Yorkshire and the Humber into the North West, so a home base within reach of that corridor is an advantage, though we will consider strong candidates anywhere in the UK.
Desirable
* Experience selling into food and drink manufacturing, or into another regulated manufacturing sector.
* Familiarity with MES, ERP, traceability, weighing or labelling systems, or with production and quality processes in a manufacturing plant.
* Experience selling a combined hardware, software and services solution rather than software alone.
* Experience opening a new market or launching a new product into an existing customer base.
* A strong existing network of contacts in food and drink manufacturing, at operations, quality, engineering or director level. If you can open doors on day one, tell us.
* Hands-on experience using AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT in a sales role, for research, drafting, call preparation or pipeline analysis.

**Role Summary**
Marex is seeking a high-calibre Capital Markets COO / Business Management professional to support the strategic development and governance of its Capital Markets business.
This front-office aligned role will work closely with Sales, Trading, Support and Control Functions, Senior Management and key infrastructure teams to drive business growth, strategic delivery, operational efficiency and regulatory readiness across the Capital Markets platform.
A primary focus of the role is to provide Corporate FX and Payments product and commercial leadership, ensuring technology priorities align with business objectives, client needs and revenue growth opportunities.
Additionally, the individual will be required to lead and coordinate various commercial initiatives, requiring strong stakeholder management, the ability to influence senior audiences, and a proven track record of delivering large-scale business change.
This is a hands-on role for someone comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment and able to juggle project execution and day-to-day business management.
**Key Responsibilities**
Business Management / COO Support
* Support the Capital Markets COO and senior business heads in the day-to-day management and strategic development of the business.
* Act as the Product/ Commercial Lead for the Corporate FX & Private Markets FX business, strategically directing and organising business requirements and technology priorities.
* Work closely with the business to build effective communication channels to understand client & user feedback of the service offering.
* Drive and coordinate key business initiatives across Capital Markets, from initial concept through to delivery and implementation.
* Act as a central point of coordination across Front Office, Operations, Technology, Legal, Compliance, Risk and Finance.
* Track and manage business priorities, strategic workstreams and change initiatives, ensuring clear ownership, governance and timely execution.
* Prepare high-quality materials for senior management, governance forums and executive stakeholders.
* Support development of scalable operating models, governance frameworks and management information.
* Ensure clear escalation and resolution of issues, risks and dependencies.
Strategic Projects and Change Delivery
* Assess new developments and client/business requests for functionality that can be presented to Technology and Management for consideration in a streamlined and efficient manner.
* Lead discussions with the business in respect of vendor consideration for tactical project delivery versus long-term internal team build.
* Hold technology accountable for quality of build and achievement of agreed delivery timelines.
* Lead or support large, business-critical initiatives, including new business launches, capability buildouts and regulatory-driven change.
* Define project scope, operating models, milestones and delivery plans across multiple stakeholders.
* Drive execution across complex, cross-functional programmes with competing priorities and dependencies.
* Ensure delivery is underpinned by strong governance, clear accountability and effective stakeholder communication.
* Influence and align stakeholders across business, infrastructure and control functions to achieve agreed outcomes.
* Support initiatives spanning product expansion, market entry, infrastructure development and process transformation.
Product, Workflow and Operating Model Support
* Champion client experience across digital channels, including client portals and interactions with client service teams.
* Work closely with front office and infrastructure teams to understand and support business activities and workflows.
* Develop a practical understanding of front-to-back processes, operating models and control frameworks.
* Support new product, new market and new workflow assessments, including process mapping, control considerations and implementation readiness.
* Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability and control across business processes.
Regulatory, Governance and Control
* Support the business in maintaining a strong governance and control environment aligned with regulatory expectations.
* Partner with Compliance, Legal, Risk and Finance on governance, regulatory and policy-related matters.
* Coordinate responses to audits, regulatory reviews and internal governance actions.
* Support the preparation of governance materials, committee papers and management reporting.
Stakeholder Management
* Create accountability for adoption and commercialisation of technology products through existing sales teams, identifying where dedicated sales resources may be required.
* Work closely with marketing on product collateral, content development and distribution channels.
* Build and maintain strong relationships across Front Office, Operations, Technology and Control Functions.
* Act as a trusted partner to senior stakeholders, balancing commercial objectives with control considerations.
* Communicate complex topics clearly and effectively to both senior and technical audiences.
* Drive alignment and consensus across stakeholders to enable effective delivery.
**Required Skills and Experience**
Core Requirements
* Commercially focused mindset with the ability to assess opportunities through a revenue-generation and business growth lens.
* Demonstrable experience in a Product, COO, Business Management, Chief of Staff, Strategy / Execution, Commercial Management or Programme Delivery role within financial services or a similarly complex, regulated environment.
* Proven track record of delivering large-scale, cross-functional business initiatives from concept through to implementation.
* Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence, challenge and align senior stakeholders across multiple functions.
* Experience coordinating delivery across Front Office, Operations, Technology, Compliance, Legal, Risk and Finance.
* Strong organisational and execution skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and drive outcomes.
* Understanding of key financial regulations (e.g. MiFID II, Payment Service Regulations)
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of materials for senior stakeholders and governance forums.
* Strong judgment, problem-solving capability and attention to detail.
Desirable
* Exposure to Capital Markets, in particular Corporate FX & Payments asset classes.
* Familiarity with:
* OTC FX across Corporate FX and Private Markets
* Payments or money movement workflows
* Collateralised and uncollateralised trading arrangements
* FX Product knowledge across (Spot, Forwards, NDFs, Options, structured products.)
* Awareness of relevant regulatory frameworks such as MiFID II and/or PSD.
Personal Competencies
* Highly organised, proactive and delivery-focused.
* Strong ability to operate under pressure and manage competing priorities.
* Commercially aware and solution-oriented.
* Confident operating with senior stakeholders.
* Able to simplify complex issues and drive practical outcomes.
* Collaborative, but willing to challenge where necessary.

## Description
**Methods Business and Digital Technology Limited**
Methods is a £100M+ IT Services Consultancy who has partnered with a range of central government departments and agencies to transform the way the public sector operates in the UK. Established over 30 years ago and UK-based, we apply our skills in transformation, delivery, and collaboration from across the Methods Group, to create end-to-end business and technical solutions that are people-centred, safe, and designed for the future.
Our human touch sets us apart from other consultancies, system integrators and software houses - with people, technology, and data at the heart of who we are, we believe in creating value and sustainability through everything we do for our clients, staff, communities, and the planet.
We support our clients in the success of their projects while working collaboratively to share skill sets and solve problems. At Methods we have fun while working hard; we are not afraid of making mistakes and learning from them.
Predominantly focused on the public-sector, Methods is now building a significant private sector client portfolio.
Methods was acquired by the Alten Group in early 2022.
**About the role**
We are looking for an experienced **Applications & Network Scrum Master** to join a major transformation programme and enable effective agile delivery across our applications and network squads.
This is a hands-on delivery role focused on creating the environment in which multidisciplinary technical teams can perform at their best. You will bring structure, transparency and momentum to delivery, helping teams maintain clear priorities, manage dependencies, remove blockers and deliver against agreed migration outcomes.
You will work closely with Product Owners, Technical Leads, Architects, Engineers, Project Managers and wider programme teams to ensure that application and network delivery remains aligned with the programme roadmap and migration waves.
The role will sit at the heart of delivery, connecting the day-to-day activity of the squads with the wider programme. You will help teams balance agile ways of working with the realities of a complex, governed transformation programme, including fixed milestones, technical dependencies, testing requirements and cutover activity.
We are looking for someone who can facilitate effectively without becoming overly process-driven; someone who can coach teams towards greater ownership and predictability while also providing constructive challenge when commitments, dependencies or delivery risks need to be addressed.
**What you will do**
As the Applications & Network Scrum Master, you will support one or more multidisciplinary squads and help establish a consistent, effective approach to agile delivery.
You will:
* Facilitate **sprint planning, daily coordination, sprint reviews, retrospectives, backlog refinement** and other agreed agile ceremonies.
* Ensure ceremonies are purposeful, inclusive and focused on achieving clear delivery outcomes rather than simply following process.
* Work with Product Owners and Technical Leads to maintain **prioritised, refined, ready and outcome-focused backlogs**.
* Help teams break down complex technical and migration activity into achievable increments that can be planned, delivered and demonstrated.
* Track delivery flow, sprint commitments, blockers, risks, dependencies and emerging issues across application and network workstreams.
* Identify impediments early and work with the appropriate teams to remove or escalate them before they impact delivery.
* Coordinate dependencies and interfaces with **identity, infrastructure, security, testing, cutover, change and other programme teams**.
* Maintain visibility of cross-squad dependencies and ensure actions and decisions are clearly owned and followed through.
* Support realistic sprint and release planning, ensuring commitments are based on team capacity, technical readiness and known dependencies.
* Encourage clear acceptance criteria, definition of ready and definition of done so that teams understand what successful delivery looks like.
* Maintain clear visibility of progress against migration waves, key milestones and programme outcomes.
* Provide timely escalation of delivery risks, blockers and dependencies where they cannot be resolved within the squad.
* Use appropriate agile metrics and delivery data to understand flow, predictability, capacity, throughput and emerging delivery trends.
* Use team feedback, retrospectives and delivery evidence to identify opportunities for **continuous improvement**.
* Coach squads in agile principles and behaviours, encouraging ownership, collaboration, transparency and continuous learning.
* Help protect delivery teams from unnecessary disruption while ensuring that programme-level commitments and governance requirements remain visible and understood.
* Work with Project Managers and Programme Leads to ensure agile delivery integrates effectively with wider programme planning, governance and reporting.
* Support the coordination of technical and operational readiness activities leading into migration and cutover events.
* Help ensure lessons learned from each delivery or migration wave are captured and used to improve subsequent waves.
**The delivery environment**
This is not a pure software-development Scrum role. You will be operating within a **complex technology transformation**, where applications, networks, infrastructure, identity, security and operational teams need to work together to deliver migration outcomes.
The squads may therefore contain a mixture of technical disciplines, and delivery will often involve dependencies that sit outside the immediate team's control.
You will need to be comfortable working in an environment where priorities can change, technical issues can emerge unexpectedly and delivery is governed by wider programme milestones.
The ability to distinguish between a genuine blocker and a problem that the team can solve themselves will be important. Equally, you will need the confidence to challenge unrealistic commitments, unclear requirements or unmanaged dependencies and ensure that issues are surfaced early rather than becoming late-stage surprises.
The successful candidate will help create a culture where **progress is visible, commitments are realistic, blockers are actively managed and teams continuously improve**.
## Requirements
**Skills and experience required**
We are looking for an experienced Scrum Master or Agile Delivery professional with a strong track record of working with multidisciplinary technical teams.
You will ideally have:
* Proven experience as a **Scrum Master, Agile Delivery Lead or equivalent**, supporting technical delivery teams.
* Strong practical experience facilitating agile ceremonies including sprint planning, daily stand-ups, reviews, retrospectives and backlog refinement.
* Demonstrable experience supporting and coaching teams to improve their agile maturity, ownership and delivery effectiveness.
* Strong backlog-management skills, with the ability to work effectively with Product Owners and Technical Leads to establish clear priorities and delivery outcomes.
* Strong experience managing **dependencies, blockers, risks, actions and impediments** across multiple teams.
* Experience working within a governed programme environment where agile teams are working towards fixed migration milestones or business deadlines.
* Practical understanding of how agile delivery operates alongside programme governance, project management, architecture, change and operational processes.
* Experience working with **applications, networks, cloud, infrastructure or other enterprise technology delivery** is strongly desirable.
* The ability to understand enough technical context to facilitate effectively and identify when an issue requires specialist intervention or escalation.
* Experience working with architects, engineers, developers, infrastructure specialists, security teams, Product Owners, Project Managers and customer stakeholders.
* Confidence using common agile planning, collaboration and reporting tools.
* Experience using delivery metrics to identify trends, improve predictability and support evidence-based conversations about delivery.
**What we are looking for in you**
You will be an excellent facilitator and communicator who can bring people together around a common outcome.
You will be comfortable asking difficult questions and providing constructive challenge without creating unnecessary friction. You will know when to coach, when to facilitate, when to intervene and when to escalate.
You will have the emotional intelligence to work effectively with different personalities, disciplines and levels of seniority, creating an environment where people feel able to raise issues and challenge assumptions.
You will also be highly organised and comfortable working across multiple workstreams. You will naturally look beyond the immediate sprint to understand how dependencies, risks and decisions could affect the wider migration programme.
Most importantly, you will be focused on **outcomes rather than ceremonies**. Agile processes are important, but your measure of success will be whether teams are becoming more predictable, dependencies are being managed effectively and the programme is successfully delivering its migration objectives.

# IRL Coordinator

IRL Coordinator
Employer:
Something Something
Category:
Music

APPLY
IRL has become a fixture of every release campaign. Most of it is terrible.
A coffee shop takeover on release day: a queue, a photo wall, a hashtag. Fans aren't silly; they can tell when something exists just because there’s something to sell. We can all do better. Not with bigger budgets, but by starting from a different question: not "what can we activate," but "what do these fans actually want, and where do they already gather?" That means listening properly - the social listening that shapes our online communities should be shaping what happens in the room. It means the announcement, the RSVP, the room and the content afterwards are one continuous piece of work. It means thinking much bigger and in the long term. An effective fan engagement campaign goes far beyond the 6-inch screen of an iPhone. Fans live in real life, so we need to meet them there. Digital content should be an extension of the world you're building, but a story truly sticks once it becomes something people can actually step inside. IRL takes the fan communities we already run online and gives them a real place to gather - listening parties, release events, meet-ups, the occasional bit of absolute chaos. Same fans, same culture - just reaching out and going beyond the screen. Once fans are in the room together, content becomes memory, marketing becomes community, and music becomes shared identity. The event lasts a few hours; the stories travel much further. This role leads that work, sitting in our Fan Engagement team with the whole studio around you. **WHAT WILL I DO?** **Listen before you build.** Our community management and amplification teams live in fans' comment sections, Discords and group chats - you'll be alongside them, using their read and our social listening to work out what a fanbase does together, where they're clustered and what they'd genuinely turn up for. That's where every idea starts. **Shape ideas, then write them up.** We create collaboratively; ideas will land from all over the studio. You'll be in those sessions, then take the strongest thinking and turn it into a proposal: concept, format, timings, activities, content deliverables, budget and how we'll measure it, and present it. **Find the rooms that already exist.** Record shops, club nights, promoters, collectives, university societies, book clubs, run clubs, and so on and so on - you'll build that network out, keep the contact book live and share it around the studio, so we're pitching from real relationships. **Produce it, properly.** Recces, venue contracts, suppliers, quotes, licensing, risk assessments, run of show, call sheets, door and guest list, and being on site when things shift (they always do!). You'll direct our production team and partners through the build, with ops behind you on contracts, insurance and budget tracking. **Build the anticipation.** Announcement moments, launch assets, RSVP and ballot mechanics, waitlists, attendee comms. **Make it travel.** Working collaboratively with the team for shot lists, photographer and videographer briefs, live posting, and an amplification plan so the best moments are live before we’re even done for the night. **Feed it back.** Post-event reviews the whole team learns from: attendance, content performance, what fans shared unprompted, what fell flat, what we'd do differently. IRL is a discipline we're building here, and you'll have a big hand in shaping it. **WHO ARE YOU?** **A fan, first.** You understand why people queue for hours, travel across the country or post 20 stories from the same event. You know the best fan experiences aren't always the biggest - they're the ones that make people feel part of something. **A producer.** You genuinely enjoy making complicated things happen. Timelines, suppliers, venues and logistics don't overwhelm you - they're puzzles you like solving. **Social-first.** You instinctively think, "how will this live online?" while everyone else is still deciding where to put the bar. **Organised.** Events rarely go exactly to plan. You stay organised when everyone else is running around. **Collaborative.** You'll spend your week bouncing between strategists, creatives, producers, artists and clients. You enjoy making other people's ideas happen. **Curious.** The first event shouldn't look like the tenth. You're always looking for new formats, new technologies and better ways to surprise fans. **What’s in it for You?**
* **Salary:** £32,000 - 39,000K
* **Unlimited Annual Leave:** With tracking and support to ensure a minimum of 28 days per year.
* **Generous Pension Contributions:** 2:1 employer match on pension contributions.
* **Career Progression:** A clear path to grow with the company and develop your role over time.
* **Hybrid Working:** Two days in the office per week, based in East London, with the option to work remotely.
* **Overtime Pay:** Extra for the late nights, content shoots, weekend festivals.
* **Regular Event Invites:** Festivals, gigs, networking, the proper stuff.
* **Vibrant Work Culture:** A team that actually likes each other and takes the work (not themselves) seriously.
**Who Are We?** Something Something is the digital-native content strategy studio. We're a collective of social strategists and content producers who believe the voices we love deserve to be heard clearly amongst the noise. Working directly with music artists and cultural brands, we know what's happening online before it's even "happening", not because we study trends, but because we live them. We don't believe in artists working for trends; we believe in making trends work for them. And we measure success in worldbuilding and real fandom, not just like counts. **Now What?** Send an email to hello@somethingsomething.social with the subject "JOB APPLICATION: IRL Coordinator". We want to hear about the time you made something happen for a community you care about. A fan event. A meet-up. A community project. Something you organised, built or brought to life, whether it was brilliantly planned or held together by a group chat and sheer determination.
Tell us what you did, and what it taught you. Maybe it sharpened your eye for logistics, taught you how to bring people together, or made you think creatively when things inevitably went a bit sideways.

# Founding Engineer, Platform & Security
Full-time · part-time considered
Remote · London preferred
Engineer #2 on the platform team. Every AI agent action Navige governs flows through a real-time interception pipeline you'll help build, harden, and scale — not a mockup, a system already running against real customer traffic.
## About the role
Navige is a real-time checkpoint AI agents pass through before they touch anything real — a governance and audit layer between an agent and the tools it calls. You'd be the second engineer on the platform, working directly with the founder from day one.
This isn't a greenfield pitch. The core pipeline is live: a Fastify gateway intercepting Model Context Protocol tool calls and a generic real-time enforcement endpoint for anything else, a deterministic policy engine (no LLM in the decision path — every allow/deny/approve decision is reproducible, on purpose), an append-only audit ledger, and optional tamper-evident anchoring to Polygon. A Next.js dashboard, Salesforce/Agentforce integration, and self-serve billing are shipped and running against real customer data.
## What you'll work on
* The interception pipeline itself: policy evaluation, kill switches, blast-radius rate limiting, approval workflows — the parts that have to be correct, not just fast
* Extending real-time governance to more integration surfaces beyond MCP and Salesforce
* Real infrastructure work: Postgres schema and partitioning at scale, Redis-backed rate limiting, deployment and observability across Railway and Vercel
* Direct ownership — the architecture decisions you make become the company's architecture, not a proposal that goes through review
## What we're looking for
* 4+ years in production TypeScript/Node.js
* Comfortable owning a system end to end — API design, database schema, deployment, the incident when something breaks at 2am
* A distributed-systems or security background is a strong signal, not a requirement
* You care about correctness in systems that make real decisions with real consequences — this is a product where "probably right" isn't good enough
Current stack: TypeScript, Node 22, Fastify, Next.js, Postgres (Drizzle), Redis, pnpm workspaces, Railway, Vercel.

# Project Manager Career Programme with Job Guarantee, Live Training and Certifications
## Become a Project Manager
No experience needed. Average UK project manager salaries reach £54,780, over 41% above the national average.
## Course Overview
Project management is one of the most accessible well paid careers in the UK for someone changing direction, because it rewards organisation, judgement and communication more than it rewards a technical background. What it does demand is proof. Employers hiring a project manager need to see that you know the method, the vocabulary, and the tools before they will hand you a budget and a team.
Our Project Manager career programme is built to give you that proof. Over eight modules you will earn four recognised certifications, learn the two ways UK projects actually get delivered, and build the practical tool skills that appear in almost every project manager job description. You will be taught live by an instructor rather than left alone with a video library, and when your training is complete our recruitment team takes over and works with you until you are placed.
The programme is designed for people with no project management background at all. If you have ever run an event, coordinated a team, managed a budget or kept a complicated thing on schedule, you already have the instincts. This programme gives them a name that employers recognise.
On completion of our job guarantee career programmes, we work with you to rebuild your CV into a compelling marketing document that employers want to read, provide you with interview and professional skills training and coaching, and help you build your job search while we map market opportunities for you and introduce you to our network of clients.
### 1. Excel with AI
Live instructor led
Practical Excel skills for modern project professionals. Developed by Newto Training.
Covers spreadsheet skills as a project professional actually uses them, including structuring data properly, formulas, lookups, pivot tables, charts and trackers - and then layers on how AI tools inside and alongside Excel change that work.
Modern Excel can draft formulas from a plain-English description, explain an inherited formula someone else built, summarise a dataset, spot trends and outliers, and build charts and pivot tables from a prompt.
### 2. PL-300: Microsoft Power BI
Live instructor led. Includes the official Microsoft exam.
PL-300 teaches you to answer it with data rather than opinion. You will learn to pull information from different sources, clean and model it, and turn it into dashboards and reports that senior stakeholders can read at a glance.
The module covers preparing data, modelling it, visualising and analysing it, and managing and securing what you publish. For a project manager this is what turns a status report from a list of assertions into something defensible. It is also the certification that most clearly separates you from other candidates at interview, because very few entry level project managers arrive able to build their own reporting.
### 3. PRINCE2 Foundation
Live instructor led. Includes the official PeopleCert exam.
PRINCE2 is the UK project management standard across major industries. Foundation teaches you the language.
You will cover the seven principles, seven practices - business case, organising, quality, plans, risk, issues and progress - and seven processes from start-up to proper closure. You will also learn what each management product is for and who is accountable for what.
There are no prerequisites. This is the genuine open door into the profession, and the point at which your existing experience acquires a vocabulary that recruiters recognise.
### 4. Microsoft Project
Live instructor led
Knowing the method is one thing. Building the schedule is another, and it is what you will be asked to demonstrate in an interview for a waterfall delivery role.
This module takes you through the Microsoft Project environment and then into real scheduling: task durations, milestones, manual and automatic scheduling, task relationships and dependencies, and identifying the critical path. You will move on to managing resources, resolving over allocation, resource levelling, part time resource calendars and overtime, and then into costs, covering variable costs, per usage and fixed costs, and changing rates part way through a project.
By the end you can take a set of requirements and produce a defensible plan with a critical path, a resourced timeline and a cost profile. That is the single most requested practical skill in UK waterfall project manager job adverts.
### 5. Risk Management
Self paced e-learning
Risk is the part of the job that separates a project manager who is trusted from one who is merely tolerated.
This module covers what risk actually is, how to describe it properly, why risk management fails, the common barriers to doing it well, and where corporate governance and internal control fit in.
You will then work through risk management principles and their outcomes, and finally the practical documents: the risk management policy and process guide, risk strategy, issue register, risk improvement plan, risk communications plan, risk response plan and risk progress reports, and how all of them relate to each other.
This module sits deliberately alongside the PRINCE2 risk practice. PRINCE2 tells you that risk must be managed. This module shows you how it is done in a real organisation.
This module is about the human side of delivery, which is the side almost no entry level project manager has been trained in.
You will cover the change process and its impact, including the learning dip and the cycle of competence, and then four approaches to change: behavioural, cognitive, psychodynamic including the change curve, and humanistic, taking in Herzberg and Maslow along the way. From there you move into personality and change, covering Lewin's three step model, communication during change, Tuckman's stages of team development and Belbin team roles, and then into organisational culture, Morgan's organisational metaphors and how culture shapes which change approach will work.
The final section covers leaders and managers, leadership styles including Goleman's, transformational versus transactional leadership, dispersed leadership, and how to sustain change once the project team has moved on.
### 7. PRINCE2 Practitioner
Live instructor led. Includes the official PeopleCert exam.
Practitioner proves you can run a project, not just support one. It is the qualification that helps a CV move from project support to full project manager roles.
You will learn to tailor PRINCE2 to a project's size, risk and complexity, select the right management products, manage change control and tolerances, and use a live business case to make genuine go/no-go decisions.
This is the step in the programme that moves you from supporting projects to being accountable for one.
This module makes sure the answer is both. You will cover the agile mindset and how to blend agile ways of working with PRINCE2 governance, which is what hybrid delivery actually looks like in a large UK organisation. It also covers agile roles and duties, stakeholder engagement, agile leadership basics, risk and change control in fast moving environments, progress tracking with agile appropriate metrics, value driven thinking and how agile is scaled across an organisation.
This module is deliberately last. Once you understand structured delivery properly, agile stops looking like a different religion and starts looking like a set of tools you can choose from. That is exactly how experienced project managers talk about it, and it is how you want to sound in an interview.

## **The Role**
We’re looking for a well-connected, highly capablle VP, Market Intelligence, to own Nscale’s view of the data centre market and act as our first point of contact for third-party DC capacity, and in many cases for land and power opportunities, across EMEA.
Reporting to the SVP Development, EMEA, and a senior member of the DCI team, you will drive our expansion strategy in existing and new markets and build the supplier relationships that give Nscale the best pool of supply options. ## **Key Responsibilities**
* Market Intelligence: Own Nscale’s view of the data centre industry, providing leading insight on industry-wide and individual market trends, the development pipeline by market and operator, and competitor capacity, contracts and strategy.

### Project Manager - Defence Virtual Simulation (FAR)
Global Program Management - Farnborough, Hampshire (Hybrid)

We are a well-established team based in Farnborough (UK) at OneArc, developing world-leading military simulations for major NATO powers and their allies. We constantly seek ways to advance the industry using the latest technologies and trends (such as whole-world simulations, motion tracking, VR, and AR).
We believe in saving lives through simulations.
Your job will be totally different from what you expect
We give you freedom and responsibility to do things well, support you, train you, and teach you. We have a relaxed environment where we aim not to limit our staff with too many regulations. We trust you.
We offer a wide variety of work and a crunch-free environment due to our products being developed as a continuous service.
Also, you will not constantly do the same things over and over again.
About the role
You will be the boots-on-the-ground face of our flagship Defence Virtual Simulation (DVS) programme for the UK Ministry of Defence (UK MOD) — travelling regularly to units across the country to support, train, and build relationships with the people actually using our software.
This is a frontline, relationship-first role first, and a project management role second. You'll work with personnel at every level — from a corporal needing basic IT assistance through to a brigadier overseeing a complex training exercise — and represent OneArc confidently in front of a room, whether that's a customer course, a conference, or a symposium.
Over your first year, and with our support, you'll grow into providing PM support and managing smaller UK-based projects — including time and backing to work towards a PMQ or PRINCE2 qualification if you don't already hold one. There's no expectation you arrive with deep project management experience; what matters is that you're excited to get out on the road, learn how different parts of the armed forces work, and help them get the most out of our software.
Our business has a worthy cause — the work we do has an actual impact on making the world a safer place. You will serve as a key point of contact between UK MOD units, internal teams, and industry partners, helping drive adoption of our software, supporting customer satisfaction, organising community events, and supporting sales opportunities.
Do you think you have what it takes?
* Ideally, you've served in the military, or you have industry experience within a defence-focused organisation (for example, another defence company involved in service delivery) — either way, you understand how different parts of the armed forces operate and how they might use simulation and training software. Exposure across multiple service branches is a strong plus.
* You're comfortable working with people at every level of the military — from a corporal needing basic IT assistance through to a brigadier overseeing a complex training exercise.
* You have strong public speaking skills and are confident standing up in front of a customer course, conference, or symposium to talk about simulation and training.
* You're early in your career rather than in a senior role — for example, not long out of the Army, or around five years into industry — and you're excited to travel to units across the country to support them and learn their use cases.
* You proactively take on complex challenges and work to get them fixed, aiming for long-term operational success.
* You take ownership of your work, adapt to changing requirements, and are self-motivated and highly organised.
* You hold, or are eligible to obtain, UK security clearance.
* Formal project management experience isn't required from day one — but you should have worked in or alongside projects in some capacity. Over your first year, you'll build towards providing PM support and managing smaller UK-based projects, with support to complete a PMQ (APM) or PRINCE2 Practitioner qualification along the way if needed.
* You should be located in Southern England - Hybrid working with the requirement to attend customer sites across the UK, as well as the OneArc Farnborough office when required.
Nice to have
* Hands-on Virtual Battlespace (VBS) experience — e.g. Administrator course completion and regular active usage.
* ITIL qualification.
* In-depth knowledge of computer hardware, software, and software development lifecycles.
* Familiarity with military simulation, interoperability standards, and military R&D.
* Detailed knowledge of the broader VBS product suite.
* High proficiency in Microsoft Excel and dedicated project planning software.
What you get?
We're not about all the hard work and no fun. Our office culture is relaxed, collaborative, and mission-driven. We do our best to look after our people.
Below is a snapshot of the perks you'll get if you work with us:
* A diverse, challenging, yet fun working life — travelling to and supporting one of the UK MOD's most critical simulation programmes.
* The opportunity to work on top-of-the-line, cutting-edge products employed by military organisations globally.
* The ability to build the OneArc brand across the armed forces, influence programme direction, and directly impact capability rollout.
* Structured growth into a project management remit over your first year, backed by qualification support.
* Work with and learn from talented colleagues in a high-visibility, customer-facing role.
* Full-time employment with a competitive salary.
* Hybrid working on office days: 3 days office, 2 days home option (in addition to regular UK travel).
* 25 days vacation per year + 8 bank holidays.
* 5% company pension contribution matching scheme.
* Death in Service Life Assurance benefit (3x annual salary).
* Free gym access scheme.
* Office refreshments including filtered water, coffee, tea, and fruit.
We don't offer just a job. We want to give you the opportunity to grow and advance the simulation market.

# Senior Applied AI Engineer (Private Sector Contractor)
**Hybrid**Full time

OverviewApplication
## Description
**Role: Senior Applied AI Engineer (Private Sector Contractor)**
**Rate: £700–£900 per day, dependent on experience**
**Location: Hybrid: 2 days a week on site at Harwell, Oxfordshire; remainder remote (UK-based)**
**Engagement: Contract, outside IR35: initial [6]-month term with strong likelihood of extension**
**Start: Immediate Start**
### A note from the Founders
***Oxford Dynamics is at an inflection point.***
We build frontier AI for environments where the cost of a wrong decision is high: defence and national security, critical infrastructure, and commercial organisations making high-stakes decisions on complex data. We are growing fast, and the constraint on how fast is no longer ideas or opportunity. It is whether the systems we ship are good enough for the people who stake decisions on them.
That is where you come in. We need engineers who can build the systems this mission depends on, and build them to a standard that holds when the answer has to be right. You will be trusted to own real systems end-to-end, held to a single high standard, and judged on one thing above all: whether what you ship earns the confidence people place in it when the decision matters.
If you are the kind of engineer who builds rather than assembles, who wants your work measured by whether it holds up in production rather than whether it demos well, and who wants to see the direct line from your code to systems people depend on, we would love to hear from you.
### Who We Are
Founded in 2019, Oxford Dynamics is a fast-growing UK frontier technology company developing both digital and physical AI systems built to operate in dynamic, mission-critical environments.
At the core of everything we build is AVISTM (A Very Intelligent System), our orchestration platform: the intelligence layer that fuses multi-modal data, including text, imagery, telemetry and sensor feeds, so operators can interrogate complex information at speed and make better decisions under pressure. AVISTM powers our digital decision products, such as ORION for multi-source decision-to-effect, and it powers our physical platforms.
We work where wrong decisions can be catastrophic. We partner with defence, security and private sector organisations internationally to bring frontier AI into the environments where it matters most, whether that is protecting nations, infrastructure and lives, or transforming how commercial organisations reason over their data and make high-stakes decisions.
## Requirements
As a Senior Applied AI Engineer at Oxford Dynamics, you will build and ship agentic AI systems in production: designing the multi-agent pipelines, the reasoning and retrieval, the model integration, and the infrastructure that carries them into production. These are systems people rely on to make consequential decisions, so what you build has to earn its confidence honestly and hold up under scrutiny.
This is a builder's role, not an integrator's, and it is unambiguously senior. We need an engineer who designs and implements systems rather than wiring together off-the-shelf parts, who takes technical ownership of the workstream and sets the direction other engineers build to. You will make systems-level design decisions, write production-grade code, and own the hard engineering that makes agentic AI reliable in demanding production environments, including secure, on-premises and offline deployments, from architecture through to deployment.
That ownership is real. You will own features end-to-end and be accountable for how they behave under pressure, not just whether they work on your machine. Reliability, latency and failure behaviour are your concern rather than an afterthought, because in the environments we deploy into, reliability and trust matter more than speed to market.
Frontier here means dependable, not experimental. You need the engineering depth to build systems that keep working under real-world conditions, whether that is heavy load, degraded connectivity or a fully offline environment, and the judgement to know the difference between a demo and a system someone can stake a decision on.
### Key Responsibilities
• **Build the systems themselves.** You design and build multi-agent AI systems from the ground up, using frameworks such as LangGraph or Haystack where they help, and building the orchestration, state and tool-calling infrastructure underneath them when they do not.
• **Engineer for production.** You write clean, tested, maintainable code and make sound systems-level decisions, treating reliability, latency and failure behaviour as first-class concerns.
• **Put models to work.** You integrate large language and vision-language models into real reasoning, search, summarisation and task-execution pipelines, and build the retrieval, memory and guardrails that make them dependable.
• **Deploy where it is hard.** You take systems into cloud, on-premises and, where required, fully offline environments, and engineer for the security and reliability constraints that come with each.
• **Own the full pipeline.** You build production pipelines from data ingestion through to inference, owning the whole path rather than a slice of it.
• **Make confidence earned, not asserted.** You build the evaluation, observability and guardrails that show how a system actually behaves, its agent behaviour, model performance and failure modes.
• **Set the technical bar.** You act as a technical authority for agentic AI, taking technical ownership of the workstream, setting the design patterns and direction other engineers build to, and leaving behind systems and documentation the team can maintain after your engagement ends.
### What We're Looking For
• Significant professional software engineering experience (typically 6+ years), including several years building LLM-based or agentic systems, with a demonstrable track record as a senior or lead engineer.
• Strong software engineering fundamentals: you write clean, tested, production-grade code and make sound systems-level design decisions, not just working prototypes.
• Commercial experience building multi-agent or agentic AI systems in production, owning them as an engineer rather than integrating them as a user.
• Strong Python, with hands-on experience building on LLM frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, Haystack, or similar) and the ability to work below the framework when you need to.
• Experience designing and deploying AI/ML systems into real production environments, not just notebooks or demos.
• A solid grasp of the engineering around models: inference, latency and performance, data pipelines, state and memory, and tool or function calling.
• Hands-on experience building search and retrieval over very large multi-modal datasets (3TB+ of text, imagery, telemetry and sensor data): indexing, embedding and querying at that scale, and feeding the results into LLM or agentic pipelines with the latency and precision they need to be useful.
• Fluency with Docker, Git and cloud platforms (AWS preferred).
• Understanding of secure deployment patterns: air-gapped, on-premises or sovereign cloud.
• A builder's mindset: you ship real, dependable systems and can explain them clearly to technical and non-technical people alike.
• Senior technical ownership: you own your delivery end-to-end, take technical ownership of the workstream, and set the direction other engineers build to. You are disciplined about documentation and knowledge transfer so what you build outlives your engagement.
### Nice to Have
• Experience with multimodal reasoning
• Experience with edge or offline AI deployments
• Familiarity with Kubernetes (EKS/OpenShift) for managing deployed applications
• MLOps experience: model evaluation, monitoring, reproducibility
• Observability tooling for agentic systems (model drift, agent behaviour, performance monitoring)
• Experience with agent orchestration patterns and inter-agent communication protocols (e.g. A2A)
• Familiarity with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool and context integration in agentic systems
• Familiarity with secure-by-design development principles (ISO 27001, NIST, OWASP)
• Experience in defence, national security, or similarly regulated environments
• Contributions to open-source AI/ML projects
### Why This Role?
This is a role for engineers who want to build things that matter and see where they land. You will own real systems end-to-end, work at the frontier of agentic and generative AI, and see your work deployed with organisations where getting the answer right matters. Few engineering roles let you say that the thing you built is trusted by people making consequential decisions. If you build to a high bar and want your work to count, we would love to meet you.
## Benefits
### Why Oxford Dynamics?
Join one of the most exciting, fastest-growing areas in the world: the convergence of AI and robotics. Every member of the Oxford Dynamics team has a major impact on the products and services we provide. Regardless of job title, you will make a real difference and learn from colleagues across every area of our business.
### What We Offer
• Competitive day rate, dependent on experience
• Genuine technical ownership and the scope to shape architecture, not just deliver tickets
• The opportunity to work with a fast-growing, successful early-stage business, with a realistic prospect of extension or a longer-term arrangement
• Flexible and hybrid working pattern
*Oxford Dynamics is committed to creating an inclusive team experience for all. Regardless of race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, age, disability, or parental status, we believe our work is at its best when everyone feels free to be their authentic self.*

Our charter is simple to state and ambitious to deliver: build what Pearson does next. We are a small, newly formed team within Pearson's Enterprise Learning & Skills (ELS) division, creating entirely new products for our enterprise clients rather than improving existing ones.
Our starting point is an asset few companies can claim. Pearson has nearly two centuries of history and, with it, one of the world's deepest bodies of learning content, assessment data, and credentialing expertise. AI has transformed what that heritage makes possible. Our mission is to bring it to bear in new and distinctive ways - solving problems for our customers that could not be solved before AI.
That charter is intentionally broad. Each product may address a different challenge for the organizations we serve, but everything we build shares three characteristics:
* **It will always involve integrations.** Our products operate inside our clients' ecosystems - learning platforms, HR systems, identity providers, and data pipelines - and must work seamlessly with all of them.
* **It will almost always build on other Pearson products.** Pearson's portfolio spans assessment, qualifications, credentials, learning content, and workforce skills. We combine these capabilities - and the data and insight behind them - in ways that were not possible before, collaborating across the company as much as within the team.
* **It will be researched and validated before it scales.** We take an evidence-led approach: concepts are tested with real customers, and only those that prove their value move forward. Some ideas will be retired and others will advance - both outcomes are signs of a disciplined process.
The team is built around senior individual contributors - design engineers, product engineers, and a zero-to-one product manager - who work as peers from initial concept to shipped product.
**The role**
You think like a designer and build like an engineer. As a Senior Design Engineer on this team, you'll take new product concepts from first sketch to interactive prototype to production-quality interface — sometimes in the same week. There's no handoff here: you design in Figma, in code, and in whatever AI tool gets you to the answer fastest, then put the result in front of real users at real enterprise clients.
This is a senior individual contributor role. There are no direct reports; your influence comes from craft, evidence, and trust.

* Prototype new product concepts in code (React/TypeScript or similar) at whatever fidelity the question demands — from disposable spikes to polished, demo-ready experiences used in client validation.
